name: Context7
verdict: A focused way to pull current library documentation into coding-agent context instead of relying on stale model memory.
bestFor: Current library documentation in agent workflows
caveat: Documentation can still be versioned, incomplete or ambiguous. Source and version remain worth checking on critical changes.

name: CodeRabbit
verdict: Useful when AI review is inserted into an existing pull-request process instead of becoming a second, disconnected coding surface.
caveat: Comments are suggestions. Repository permissions, false positives and high-risk changes still need human ownership.

name: Momentic
verdict: Interesting because it targets real browser paths and maintenance overhead rather than treating testing as prompt-generated boilerplate.
caveat: Payment, auth and other critical flows still benefit from deterministic assertions and explicit isolation.

name: Semgrep
verdict: A strong counterweight to generic AI code review because rules and findings remain inspectable at the code level.
caveat: Rules and severity need project-specific tuning; scanner output is not the same thing as resolved risk.

name: Dovetail
verdict: Most useful when the AI layer keeps customer-research evidence traceable instead of collapsing interviews into uncheckable summaries.
caveat: Thin or biased research does not become valid because an AI layer can summarize it faster.

name: Relume
verdict: Worth watching because it starts from structure and reusable components rather than treating a one-shot visual generation as the finished product.
caveat: Brand direction, editorial judgement and unusual interaction design still need deliberate human work.
